name: Gus Bradley

views.text: Great effort and great enthusiasm create energy on the field, and energy wins downs.
A simple defense played fast beats a clever one played slow.
Players should hear the truth every day, good or bad; consistency is how a coach earns credibility.
Point out what went right so it gets repeated, not just what went wrong.
Linebackers who used to be safeties see the coverage picture faster.
Keep a staff together across stops; trust built over years is worth more than any new idea.
Running the defense during the week while the head coach calls it on Sunday works when the standard is shared.

signatures: stays relentlessly upbeat at the podium even after a rough defensive day
talks about effort and enthusiasm before he talks about scheme
calls himself an optimist when asked about a rebuild
want: to help his old friend build one more fast, energetic defense, and prove his best coaching is not behind him
fear: that his positivity is remembered as softness because his records as a head coach and later coordinator fell short
voice: Warm, upbeat and earnest; he speaks about effort, enthusiasm, honesty and consistency, avoids criticizing players publicly, and keeps a positive tone even when the numbers are bad. Comfortable in a supporting role beside a play-calling head coach.

evidence.summary: Jacksonville fires Bradley after a ninth straight loss leaves the team 2-12 and him 14-48 over three-plus seasons; he came from Seattle as defensive coordinator; coverage notes his always-positive approach. Date taken from the firing; the AP story itself is a firing report.

Introduced as coordinator, Bradley wants great effort and great enthusiasm, says enthusiasm creates energy and pressure can restore it, describes a simple, Cover 3-based scheme stressing toughness and communication, and gives players a blank slate. Measured, confident tone; team-written.
John Fox joins as senior defensive assistant and calls Bradley an outstanding teacher; notes that Bradley and several assistants have worked together at multiple stops. Testimony from a colleague.

Team feature on his first season: players say he set a clear standard and lives by it through Richardson's season-ending injury, a suspension and a three-game skid; Tyquan Lewis says he brought accountability; Blackmon says players trust the plan; DC Gus Bradley praises his steady message and that he holds players and coaches alike to the standard. Team-written.

Indianapolis fires Bradley after three seasons without a playoff berth as the defense allowed the third-, fifth- and ninth-most points and regressed in yards and sacks; Steichen calls him a man of great character whom he respects. Firing report.

Introduction: wants a fast, violent defense without a huge menu of calls, with complexity never at the cost of identity; believes consistency and honest feedback build credibility, highlights what went right so it is repeated, and stresses accountability; longtime friend of Saleh, who calls the defense on game days; calls himself an optimist. 37th year coaching, eighth NFL franchise. Team-written.
Camp note: speaks glowingly of a linebacker with a safety background and says the Titans like such linebackers for their instincts in coverage. One item.

review.notes: Moved seat 2026 (IND DC to 2024, SF assistant head coach 2025, now TEN DC under a play-calling Saleh). Added 2026 sources E6-E7 (introduction, camp). Views and voice updated for the non-play-calling role; new tie to Saleh. Sliders unchanged; 2026 coverage of him is light.
